title: AgentShield Policy
description: Schema for AgentShield policy.yaml and pack YAML files. Backs editor intellisense (VS Code's yaml.schemas, JetBrains, neovim/coc.nvim) and is regression-tested against the Go types via internal/policy/schema_test.go.

disable_rules.description: Rule IDs to skip at evaluation. Managed mode ignores user disables for community rules. Use `agentshield rule disable <id>` to add entries safely.

decision.description: BLOCK rejects the command. AUDIT executes but logs as flagged. ALLOW executes normally. REQUIRE_APPROVAL pauses and asks for confirmation before running (internal/policy/types.go DecisionRequireApproval); #3298 tracks it still resolving to allow on harnesses with no native approval channel. This is the exhaustive list the engine acts on — internal/policy/schema_test.go pins it against the Decision constants.

protected_paths.description: Glob patterns for paths that any command attempting to read/write triggers a BLOCK. Tilde expands to $HOME. A path used only in a designated consumer's credential slot (see protected_path_consumers) is recorded as AUDIT instead.

protected_path_consumers.description: Executables that may take a protected path as a credential. A protected path that appears ONLY as one of these consumers' flag values (or as a positional operand when positional is true) yields AUDIT with rule id protected-path-consumer instead of BLOCK. An assignment of a protected path to one of the consumer's env names is recorded the same way, and never blocked. Additive on merge.

flags.description: Flags whose value is the credential: next word, or --flag=value. A short flag matches as the last letter of a cluster (-vi).

positional.description: Allow the credential as a bare operand (ssh-add ~/.ssh/id). Never set for tools that can copy the file out (scp, rsync).

env.description: Environment variables that ARE this consumer's credential slot (KUBECONFIG, AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE). Assigning a protected path to one is recorded as protected-path-consumer AUDIT, never blocked; matched case-sensitively. Unlike flags this is not tied to executable — the assignment and the use are routinely separate commands.

allow_domains.description: Allowed outbound destinations. Enforced only when enforce_allowlist is true, and then only the entries in your own policy file count (not the built-in defaults or pack domains). An entry matches the host and its subdomains; *.host matches subdomains only; an IP address matches only itself.

enforce_allowlist.description: Opt-in outbound allowlist (#4437). When true, a network command whose destination Shield can name (curl, wget, URL remotes of git clone/fetch/pull/push/ls-remote) is blocked when the host is not on allow_domains (subdomains included); destinations Shield cannot name are recorded, not stopped. Loopback (localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1) is never blocked. Absent or false changes no decision. A value that is not true/false leaves it off with a warning.

id.description: Unique rule ID. Convention: ts-/sc-/co-/cred- prefix by kingdom.

rule_tests.description: Inline TP/TN/attested cases. TP commands MUST fire the rule; TN commands must NOT fire it; attested commands MUST fire AND come out at AUDIT via a command_intent_downgrade label (#2843/#2983). Validated by go test ./internal/policy -run TestRuleYAMLTests.

attested.description: Commands on which the rule fires (is attributed) but a command_intent_downgrade label moves BLOCK/REQUIRE_APPROVAL to an attested AUDIT: doc-text and heredoc positions. Requires command_intent_downgrade on the rule.

match.description: Exactly one match shape per rule (regex/structural/dataflow/semantic/stateful). Combining is allowed but unusual.

command_regex_exclude.description: Regex that, if matched, suppresses this rule (FP escape hatch).

command_intent_exclude.description: Suppress this rule when the command carries any of these intent labels (set by IntentClassifier). Replaces {{DOC_CONTEXT}} for new rules; unknown label names are rejected at policy load.

command_intent_downgrade.description: Downgrade this rule's BLOCK/REQUIRE_APPROVAL to AUDIT (instead of suppressing it) when the match sits only in statements carrying any of these intent labels — e.g. a sensitive literal inside a gh/git --body/--message argument (#2843). Same per-statement scoping as command_intent_exclude; the finding is still AUDITed, so there is no false negative.

command_position_exclude.description: Suppress this rule when its match exists ONLY at one of these syntactic positions. Different question from command_intent_exclude: an intent label classifies the whole command's text, a position label asks where the match landed in the parsed command. loop_wordlist = an item of a `for NAME in …` word list whose loop variable is only printed or used as a search pattern — the value is data being iterated, not an operand (#3376). search_needle = the PATTERN operand of a grep-family invocation (grep/egrep/fgrep/rg/ag) — a search term compared against file content, never a target being opened, executed, or attached to (#3382); withdrawn when the command executes grep's output, whose every line contains the needle (#4468). heredoc_body = the BODY text of a `cat`/`tee <<DELIM … DELIM` heredoc — data being written or printed, never a command-line token; never applies to a heredoc fed to an interpreter (bash/sh/python3/…), whose body is code (#3397). Position alone is not the exemption: `for p in /etc/shadow; do cat "$p"; done` still fires, and a genuine invocation appearing anywhere else in the command still fires. Unknown labels are rejected at policy load.

command_fold_separators.description: Also match the command with Unicode separators (U+00A0 and the other Zs/Zl/Zp characters) folded to a space (#4310). For rules whose pattern matches PROSE an LLM later reads: RE2's \s is ASCII-only, so one NBSP between the words of a directive drops the rule while the model reads ordinary words. Additive (the raw reading is tried first). Never set on a rule that matches shell syntax: NBSP is not a word separator to bash.

powershell_strings.description: Some string literal the PowerShell lane read outside every command's elements (assignments, arrays, hashtables, redirection targets, .NET method arguments) equals one entry, ASCII case-insensitively. For .NET text with no command (the AMSI bypass). A sibling of powershell, never combined with any matcher; older binaries decode it as an empty match.

powershell_calls.description: A powershell match whose tree may also name .NET method calls (call nodes): a network cmdlet fed by [Convert]::ToBase64String(...), or [Microsoft.Win32.Registry]::SetValue(...) on its own. A sibling of powershell, never combined with any matcher; v0.2.2619 to v0.2.2640 decode it as an empty match, so premium rules may use it. Call nodes are valid only here.

powershell_match.description: Match one command the PowerShell lane read (ADR-001 step 5), or, under powershell_calls, one .NET method call (a call node). Evaluated only by the PowerShell lane; a rule with this block may carry no other matcher, so the bash pipeline never reads it. Every field given must hold for the same command or call.

command.description: Canonical command names, aliases resolved by the lane (iex is invoke-expression). Exact and ASCII case-insensitive, never a prefix; a native program matches with or without a directory and .exe; any reading of a version-dependent alias matches.

call.description: Makes this node a call node (valid only under powershell_calls): a .NET method call, Type::Method for a static call (the type as written, with or without System., ASCII case-insensitive) or .Method for an instance call on any object. A call node names no command and carries only values_any (over the string literals in its arguments) and fed_by_any (the commands and calls inside its arguments).

params_any.description: Some parameter of the command matches one entry.

positions.description: The parameters the command binds positional arguments to, in order (Set-ItemProperty: -Path, -Name, -Value); params_any then also reads a parameter bound by position. Only widens params_any, so a binary that predates it reads the rule as written without it.

args_any.description: Some word of the command equals one entry (ASCII case-insensitive): an argument's value, or a parameter as written (a native program receives -create as a word). A parameter's attached value (-Name:x) and each item of an array value (a,b) are words too.

args_wildcard.description: args_any also matches a word that is a PowerShell wildcard pattern (*, ?, [a-c], backtick escapes) matching an entry, for a command that expands one (Stop-Service -Name WinDef*). Only widens args_any, so a binary that predates it reads the rule as written without it.

paths_any.description: Some whole-value path of the command matches one glob (ASCII case-insensitive). A leading **/ matches any trailing run of whole path components.

fed_by_any.description: Some command whose output can reach this one (an earlier stage of its pipeline, or a command inside its arguments) matches one entry. Under powershell_calls an entry may be a call node: a .NET call whose output can reach this command, or, below a call node, a command or call inside that call's arguments.

fed_by_all.description: Every entry has an input, as fed_by_any reads one: ForEach-Object fed by the Win32_ShadowCopy listing and holding the .Delete() call. A narrowing key, valid only under powershell_calls, which older binaries ignore.

encoded_command.description: The command starts PowerShell with -EncodedCommand text, in any accepted spelling, decoded or not.

stdin_script.description: The command starts PowerShell whose command line runs its standard input as the script: -, -Command -, -File -, or no script at all (only switches and options that take a value). A narrowing key, valid only under powershell_calls, which older binaries ignore.

values_any.description: Some argument value of the command (\ read as /, trailing separators dropped) matches one glob, ASCII case-insensitively; a leading **/ as in paths_any. Reads values paths_any skips as prose, such as a registry key on a provider drive. Community rules only: v0.2.2639/v0.2.2640 read a rule using it as its bare command.

powershell_output_runs.description: A file the command writes through one of params is run by a later command of the text: by its path as the command name, or as an argument of a by command. Community rules only, as values_any.

params.description: Parameters whose value is the file written: by prefix (ADR-001 decision 1), or exactly for a native long option such as --output.

by.description: Commands that run a file passed as an argument (Start-Process, msiexec, powershell -File, ...).

name.description: Matched by prefix (ADR-001 decision 1). A trailing * names a family: -Disable* matches any parameter that starts with -Disable.

value_not.description: Holds only when the parameter's value (attached with a colon, else the next argument) is none of these; a parameter with no value (a switch) holds, and so does a computed one.

context_match.description: Gate a rule on the runtime execution context (issue #3291). A precondition, not a matcher: it decides whether the rule APPLIES, so it must accompany a command_regex/command_prefix/command_exact predicate (rejected on structural/dataflow/semantic/stateful rules at load). Used to tighten posture for CI-resident, attacker-facing agents.

ci.description: true = rule applies only inside a detected CI/CD runner (execenv.Detect); false = only outside CI; omit for no CI gate.

structural_match.description: Shell-AST-aware match. Robust against flag reordering, sudo wrapping, long-form flags.

dataflow_match.description: Source→sink taint tracking. e.g., credential file → curl/wget.

semantic_match.description: Match by classified intent rather than raw command shape.

stateful_match.description: Multi-step chain match within a compound command (e.g., curl && bash).
